   Travellers can book taxi rides to JB round the clock from Nov 23 on ComfortDelGro app
 Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox
 Bookings via the Zig by ComfortDelGro app have to be made at least four hours in advance.
 PHOTO: ST FILE
 Aqil Hamzah
 Published   Nov 17, 2026, 11:20 AM
 Updated   Nov 17, 2026, 05:07 PM
 Set as preferred source Listen SINGAPORE – From Nov 23, travellers heading across the border to Johor Bahru and back can book taxi rides on the ComfortDelGro (CDG) app Zig between seven days and four hours before travel, with fixed fares shown upfront.
 Bookings can also be made through Zig’s customer service hotline at 6552-1111. The cross-border service will operate 24 hours daily.
 Cabbies will pick up fares anywhere in Singapore, with drop-offs available within a fixed area covering Johor Bahru, Iskandar Puteri and Senai.
 When returning to Singapore, travellers can head to one of three pick-up spots in Johor Bahru and, from there, go anywhere in Singapore. There will be more pick-up spots in the future.
 Zig by ComfortDelGro – a transport booking platform that brings together Singapore’s largest taxi fleet and a growing ride-hail service – in a statement on Nov 17 said it has formed a tie-up with Malaysian ride-hailing platform Kummute.
 “Under the partnership, ride requests will be fulfilled by vehicles from either network, enabling Zig and Kummute to draw on a larger combined pool of vehicles to serve customers travelling between the two cities,” it added.
 A day earlier, on Nov 16, CDG and Malaysian transport platform Kumpool – which runs Kummute – were granted licences to ferry passengers across the Causeway .
 When asked how many CDG vehicles are licensed to drive passengers between Singapore and Malaysia, a CDG spokesperson said it has 150 cross-border taxi licences.
 Kumpool director Lim Han Weng said in the statement that bringing together the two operators will help expand transport options on both sides of the border.
 In a separate statement, Kummute said it will begin accepting cross-border bookings via its platform from Dec 14. These have to be made at least two hours in advance.
 For now, those using its app have to board the vehicles at one of four designated locations if they are travelling from Singapore to Johor Bahru. These pick-up points are situated at Ban San Street Terminal, near VivoCity, near Century Square Shopping Mall, and Joo Koon.
 In May 2026, Singapore-based tech giant Grab, which offers ride-hailing and food delivery services, among other things, was the first to be awarded a licence to offer cross-border ride-hail services. With the entry of Zig by CDG and Kumpool, there are three operators.
 Prices for ride-hailing services are higher than getting a roadside taxi flag-down from the Ban San terminal near Queen Street. Ride-hail cars can pick up travellers anywhere in Singapore and ferry them to any destination within Johor Bahru, including Iskandar Puteri and Senai.
 Grab has also been shortening the advance notice needed to book such rides since it began offering the service in May.
 Initially, they needed to be booked 12 hours in advance, but a Grab spokesperson told The Straits Times that it adjusted the service after customers requested for shorter advance booking times.
 Currently, a ride to Johor Bahru on the platform can be booked 90 minutes in advance, down from 12 hours when the Grab service began.
 On Nov 16, the quota for cross-border taxis in Singapore and Malaysia was raised from 300 to 500 for each country.
 The increase marks the last stage in hitting the target of 500 licensed cross-border taxis in Singapore and Malaysia, which was first announced by the transport ministries of both countries on Dec 5, 2025.
 The move is part of efforts by both countries to strengthen cross-border connectivity and enhance the commuting experience.
 It also aims to beef up business links and people-to-people ties in Singapore and Malaysia.
